study_identification_part.si4_title: Using normative modeling to assess pharmacological treatment effect on brain state in patients with schizophrenia

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: General linear models and permutation-based Pearson correlations (n=5,000) relating deviation Z-scores (baseline/after) to PANSS dimensions; covariates: sex, age, head motion.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Two patient subgroups emerged: a normalized group with milder baseline symptoms and a deviation group; baseline depressive and overall symptoms predicted greater normalization of aFCS deviations, while baseline positive and overall symptoms predicted normalization of fFCS deviations; treatment reduced deviations in average FC more than in dynamic fluctuations.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: Normative models (10-fold CV; Cam-CAN) produced high certainty (mean 0.991 aFCS; 0.990 fFCS). In Cam-CAN, supra-deviation rates were 2.75% (aFCS) and 2.91% (fFCS); infra-deviation 2.82% (aFCS) and 2.92% (fFCS). Patients formed a ‘normalized’ subgroup (post-treatment metrics closer to normative range) and a ‘deviation’ subgroup (more extreme deviations). Baseline depressive and overall symptoms negatively predicted post-treatment aFCS deviations in dorsal/ventral attention and somatomotor networks; baseline positive and overall symptoms negatively predicted post-treatment fFCS deviations in dorsal/ventral attention, salience, control, and DMN networks. Treatment effects more consistently reduced deviations in static aFCS than dynamic fFCS.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: Sex-specific centile models using quantile regression; decomposition into Yeo-17 networks; Brainnetome atlas ROIs; sliding-window dynamic FC (60 s, step 1 s); introduced a normative certainty index from 10-fold aggregated models.

caa10_key_limitations.answer: Small sample size; reliance on 10-fold CV for healthy due to insufficient sample for independent split; out-of-sample predictions for SCZ may introduce bias; potential residual confounding despite a 2-week medication-free period.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: Parcellation: Human Brainnetome Atlas for ROI FC; networks: Yeo-17 template. Sliding window: 60 s; step 1. Preprocessing steps per SPM (MATLAB). No explicit multi-site harmonization or QC exclusion thresholds reported. Medication regimens summarized in supplement.
